name: Cyberpunk
visualIdentity: A technology-dense urban world with legible social and industrial character. Use controlled neon, atmosphere, localized reflections, and a clear luminance hierarchy; show devices, streets, or signal systems functioning. Avoid relying on purple-blue light, signs, or decorative HUDs alone. Supplemental reference, not a directly named source-collection style.
suitableUses: Explicit motion-pattern fits include product or editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, data storytelling, and cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Cyberpunk alone suits world-building; diegetic interfaces suit sci-fi trailers or speculative products. Suitability for interactive HTML is inferred from the supplied interaction patterns.
limitations: Omit chapter transitions when the topic is too short, transitions obscure causality, or cuts violate continuous-shot or loop requirements. Omit glitch for calm scenes or when it harms communication; keep it brief, bounded, readable, and non-strobing. Avoid constant corruption, cluttered HUDs, and unexplained scroll spectacle.
palette: Suggested fallback for new artwork only: background #111D25, foreground #F1F0E3, accents #52B3AC, #DAA259, #B96887. Exact task, brand, approved, and existing semantic colors take precedence; preserve values, roles, color families, and asset colors. Use discrete tokens, no gradient. Background/foreground contrast is 14.934:1; accent 3 with background is 4.398:1 and decorative only for normal text. Check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use purposeful scene motion and coherent authored trajectories while preserving deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds. Optional narrative patterns include progress-controlled chapter handoffs, staged storytelling, and brief glitch cuts; choose only scene-supported treatments. For HTML, finite scroll progress should map to reversible states, with keyboard and reduced-motion support. For video, derive state from seekable composition time, never live input; ensure direct and backward seeks reproduce the same state.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required audio layer is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience, honoring supplied assets and requirements. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and synchronize picture and sound.
assetRequirements: Build purposeful urban or technological scenes with defined light sources, fog, and PBR materials; composite readable interface text separately in SVG or HTML. Reuse suitable assets, load local fonts, seed randomness, and cache or deterministically replay stateful simulations. Do not imply simulated scenes are physical production. Required source assets are otherwise unspecified.
combinations: Diegetic interfaces (style-112) can make functioning in-world HUDs story-critical; attach each to a source, limit neon to defined lights, and keep the subject brightest. Sparse signal-intrusion transitions (style-067) can punctuate hacking or scene changes using primary accents. Avoid floating HUD clutter, purple-blue wash, constant glitch, and strobing. Cyberpunk alone is preferred for world-building.
productionApproach: Three.js handles geometry, cameras, materials, lighting, and scene rendering; PBR materials and postprocessing support believable surfaces and controlled bloom. Composite text separately. Choose motion tools by action with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is missing, recording the reason. The pipeline does not own visual style or motion design.
